slides.title: A Large Language Model-Driven Agent-Based Modeling Framework with Multi-Round Communication for Simulating Vaccine Opinion Dynamics
slides.tldr: LLM-DRIVEN AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This framework integrates LLMs into agent-based modeling to simulate cognitive processes and opinion dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: An LLM-driven agent-based framework simulates how cognitive modules like memory and prompt diversity influence vaccine opinions.
card.key_idea: Integrates Qwen3-8B into an ABM with multi-round dialogues, reflection, and react modules to model macro-level opinion dynamics and polarization among heterogeneous agents.
card.evaluation: Simulated 95 agents across four scenarios using synthetic population data. Results showed prompt diversity increased vaccination rates while memory increased resistance.
card.limitation: Small simulation scale (95 agents) due to high LLM computational costs and lack of designated opinion leaders.

slides.title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework
slides.highlight: AgoraSim enables the simulation of social reactions by mixing LLM, vision-language, and classical agents, supporting the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: AgoraSim is a hybrid agent-based modeling framework for analyzing social reactions to natural-language scenarios.
card.key_idea: It mixes LLM, VLM, and classical rule-based agents in ratio-controlled populations, projecting all behaviors into a shared structured action space for comparison against reference dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a congestion-pricing scenario walkthrough; focuses on exploratory trajectory comparison and auditability rather than predictive accuracy or formal benchmarks.
card.limitation: Does not establish external validity; synthetic agents may reflect model biases, stereotypes, or collapse toward population-typical responses.

slides.highlight: The development of ultra-realistic humanoid robots for companionship is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Multimodal Voice Activity Projection for Turn-Taking in Social Robots with Voice-Activity-Related Pretrained Encoders
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Multimodal Voice Activity Projection framework using audio-visual inputs and inter-speaker attention to predict conversational dynamics, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework for social robots to predict turn-taking by projecting future voice activity using pretrained encoders.
card.key_idea: MM-VAP uses LoRA-adapted, speech-activity-related pretrained backbones (TalkNet, WhisperFlamingo) with inter-speaker attention and a semantic consistency loss to project future voice activity states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NoXi, NoXi+J, and Haru EDR corpora using Accuracy and F1-score; outperformed baselines, especially in shift prediction.
card.limitation: The approach was not validated under real-time conditions due to high computational resource requirements of large pretrained encoders.

slides.title: HumAIN: Human-Aware Implicit Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: HumAIN uses knowledge distillation to integrate implicit social cues like gait and orientation into robot planning, enhancing socially compliant navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HumAIN enables socially compliant robot navigation by distilling privileged human skeletal cues into a vision-only model.
card.key_idea: A transformer-based teacher learns social representations from multi-modal data (RGB, skeletal keypoints, robot state), which are then distilled into a lightweight, real-time student using only RGB images.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SCAND and an OOD dataset against ViNT, NoMaD, GNM, and HST+MPC; improved trajectory metrics by an average of 29.8%.
card.limitation: Not yet robust for unconstrained open-world deployment, particularly in crowded scenes with occlusions or unexpected human behaviors.

slides.title: LLM-powered reasoning in agent-based modeling
slides.highlight: The HALE framework integrates LLMs into agent-based modeling to predict human decision-making, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: HALE integrates LLM reasoning into agent-based modeling to dynamically predict human mobility during epidemics.
card.key_idea: A hybrid framework where LLMs act as a feedback loop, adjusting agent activity networks based on demographic groups and perceived disease threat levels.
card.evaluation: Simulated COVID-19 in Salt Lake County using Llama 3.1; HALE's epidemic peak and size better matched CDC observations than ABM-only baselines.
card.limitation: LLM inference is sensitive to prompts and temperature; it lacks sufficient information for very small municipalities.

slides.title: Responsible Personalisation: The Double-Edged Sword of Personalisation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a lifecycle-based framework to analyze ethical risks in personalized human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for analyzing ethical risks of robot personalisation, emphasizing how physical embodiment amplifies these risks.
card.key_idea: A lifecycle-based, context-sensitive framework combining personalisation stages (design to end-of-life) with interaction characteristics (duration and domain) to map ethical risks and design recommendations.
card.evaluation: Based on interdisciplinary expert discussions from three workshops and a review of existing HRI/HCI literature.
card.limitation: The work provides a conceptual and analytical framework rather than empirical validation through specific robot deployments.

slides.title: A New Human-Likeness and Comfort Index for Robot Movements Along Prescribed Paths
slides.tldr: NEW INDEX FOR HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOVEMENT COMFORT
slides.highlight: This research proposes a human-likeness index based on the lognormality principle to evaluate robot trajectories, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and perceived comfort.

card.one_liner: Introduces a quantitative human-likeness index to predict robot movement comfort before execution.
card.key_idea: The index (HL) combines the Signal-to-Noise Ratio of a sigma-lognormal velocity reconstruction with a penalty for the number of strokes used.
card.evaluation: Validated with 68 subjects across three experimental campaigns; results showed a consistent trend between perceived comfort and the HL index.
card.limitation: The index is a sufficient condition; some human-like movements may have low HL values due to spinal cord adjustments.
